analysis:
Both changed files are developer documentation only (docs/developer/build.md and docs/developer/test.md). The visible changes are CI build-cache policy, CMake install from the runner tool cache, push-run routing requests to the compute plane, and a MiMo audio gate that runs only when its inputs change. No provider, coordinator, attestation, key, encryption or cache-storage source changed, so I found no regression against the threat-model assets or boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, T-041).

The test.md patch narrows CI cache saves: only pushes to dev or master save a build, and pull requests restore but save nothing. This reduces cache-poisoning exposure from PR-authored builds. The build.md excerpt covered by the supplied head text (lines 490-678) is unchanged context about the pinned SDK, the Flint native-precision settings and release runbooks, and shows no security-relevant edits. Its changed hunks (lines 170-174, 273-277, 299-382) were only visible as a truncated patch excerpt, not as numbered text.

Open items for integration. (1) Unit 67373c0eff1153bd:0 had no content supplied, so I could not examine it. (2) The build.md patch excerpt is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false) and the new 'CI Caching' section after line 299 was not visible. The documented push-run request to the compute plane and the 'branch_not_admitted' approval, along with the CMake tool-cache reuse (which skips the download when the marker and version match), describe CI workflow and script behavior that is not in the supplied evidence. Whether those behaviors are enforced or introduce CI supply-chain risk cannot be judged from docs alone. Doc claims are not proof of implementation. The related scripts and workflow files (.github/workflows, scripts/install-release-cmake.sh, scripts/ci-component-paths.py) were not supplied. These are out of the provider threat-model scope unless they affect release signing or build identity, which the docs say stay on literal Blacksmith labels.
